newsitem.title: USA: Fla. senator will try again to end portfolio tax.
newsitem.headline: Fla. senator will try again to end portfolio tax.

text.p: Florida state Sen. John Ostalkiewicz said Monday he will re-file a bill that would repeal Florida's intangibles tax on stocks and bonds and other investments.

Ostalkiewicz, R-Windermere, sought unsuccessfully during the spring legislative session to repeal the tax. His announcement that he would try again coincided with the filing deadline for intangibles tax payments.

"By midnight tonight over 628,000 Floridians will have to file returns with a government that is going to penalize them for trying to save money for their retirement, a new home or their children's education," Oskalkiewicz said.
He said the tax hurts business and stifles economic growth.

Florida is one of only a few states that still collect the tax. The U.S. Supreme Court ruled last year that North Carolina's version was unconstitutional because it taxed the stock of in-state and out-of-state companies at different rates.
Georgia, Kentucky and Michigan have recently repealed their intangibles taxes because of similar concerns.
